summary.headline: Rico Auto Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~39% to INR755 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% and PAT turned to a INR3.4 crore loss.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record INR755 crore against INR543 crore a year earlier, with aluminium casting at 89% of revenue and exports near 15%. Profitability was hit by about INR24 crore of higher other operating expenses (including air freight and sorting costs of about INR13 crore), plus an estimated INR10 crore raw-material settlement lag. Management reiterated full-year revenue of about INR3,250 crore and said margins should recover from Q3 as air freight ceases and customer price revisions flow through. Q2 margins are expected to be better than Q1 but still in between the Q1 level and the targeted trajectory.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR3,250 crore (management said more than INR3,200 crore); quarterly run-rate targets: Q2 above INR840 crore, Q3 above INR850 crore, Q4 about INR900 crore.
July 2026 turnover stated at about INR300 crore.
Full-year EBITDA margin target around 10%; management said it expects to exit the year near targeted full-year margins; Q2 margin to be between Q1 and Q3 levels.
Air freight expected to peak in Q2 and cease from Q3, with shipments returning to sea freight; progressive profitability improvement from Q3 onwards.
Management said the company will achieve its previously stated 12% margin target over time; Hosur commercial production expected September 2026.
Long-term target of about INR7,500 crore revenue by 2030 referenced by an analyst; management said about INR4,000 crore is achievable with current asset base.
capex_capacity: Hosur plant expected to start commercial production in September 2026, supporting hybrid and EV programmes; production ramp from October.
54 projects in hand; management is curbing investment and expects to invest only where absolutely necessary for about one year, then stabilise assets before larger projects.
Company has about 7-8 high-tonnage die-casting machines (1,000-2,700 ton); a 2,700-ton machine costs about INR25 crore landed plus INR10-15 crore infrastructure.
Capex guidance for FY27 and FY28 (including maintenance capex) not given; management said it will share later.
Land held for sale in Haridwar (about 2 acres, about INR10 crore) expected to be paid in full by 30 December; further land bank under discussion.
demand_pricing: Around 55 new programmes in launch phase, of which 28 launched and in ramp-up; customers include Toyota, Ford and BMW with 7-8 year programme life; company is single-source supplier on these.

Air freight incurred because ocean transit rose from 5 weeks to 9 weeks (sometimes 10 or 8) due to the West Asia conflict; customers in US and Europe; one customer agreed to pay roughly 50% of air freight cost, not yet booked.
Price increases sought from domestic and overseas customers for rupee-driven import inflation, manpower, power, fuel, gas and carbide inserts; Haryana labour cost increase of about 40% cited.
About 75% of customers (by management's statement) moved to real-time raw-material settlement; remaining 25% being onboarded.
Company does not hedge aluminium; customers announce prices. Management said aluminium prices eased slightly in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance of ~10% EBITDA margin given in June if air freight pressures were already visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transit times rose from 7 weeks assumed to 9-10 weeks; most air freight was incurred after the early-June call as the situation escalated in late June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 39% growth came from higher metal prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR100-200 crore of revenue was due to higher metal prices on a consolidated basis; standalone raw-material impact about INR100 crore, with consolidated possibly INR10-15 crore higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and full-year margin outlook and what is the path to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 margin would be between Q1 and H2 levels, with margins improving from Q3 as freight normalises and price revisions are realised; it expects to be confident of the trajectory if conditions hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aluminium price assumption behind FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the ruling price around INR320/kg (approximately INR32,000 per tonne); raw-material impact estimated at INR200-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the business reach INR4,000 crore revenue without major capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR4,000 crore plus is achievable with the current setup, with die investments largely recovered upfront from customers except for Maruti and Hero, which pay via piece price.

qa_highlights.question: Will hedging be used to manage aluminium volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company does not bank on commodities; the focus is on passing through raw-material cost via real-time settlements to eliminate the lag.

risks_watch: Air freight and sorting costs (INR12.8-13 crore in Q1) may persist into Q2; recovery from one customer (about 50% of freight) is not yet booked.
Customer settlement timing: 25% of customers not yet on real-time settlement; overseas customers may take longer to accept inflation-related price revisions.
Aluminium price volatility (about 57% higher YoY for a grade) and reliance on customer-led pricing; geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) could extend shipping times.
Quality correlation issue with a major customer put some parts on hold; rust issues from prolonged sea transit required repacking.
Margin recovery to ~10% for FY27 requires about 12-13% in H2 per analyst's arithmetic; management has not given a quarterly margin figure.
Capex, land monetisation and railway/defence revenue numbers were not fully quantified on the call.
key_quotes: This air freight is an exceptional thing and mainly because, a, it's taking almost 9 weeks for shipment from here to -- from India to the U.S.
We are very confident of what is happening. Like I mentioned about the month of July, the revenues have gone up and gone up much further than whatever we declared the last quarter.
We don't do hedging on the aluminum price because it is decided by the customers, and they are the ones who announce the price
But we can achieve a figure of about INR4,000 crores in the setup that we already have at the moment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year INR3,250 crore revenue and on margin recovery from Q3, but cautious and defensive on Q1 profitability, which management attributed to temporary air freight and the raw-material settlement lag. Answers on air-freight timing and the 10% guidance were somewhat evasive, with management repeatedly saying "let's see" and deferring exact figures (railway revenue, capex, consolidated metal impact) to later.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to more than INR3,200 crore (~INR3,250 crore), roughly 30% above the implied FY26 base, backed by 28 programmes already in ramp-up and Hosur starting September 2026, but management is curbing capex for about a year after 54 projects in hand.
